summary: Native process owner qualification at candidate c2144d52a5, the squash of rust/s05-native-process-qual (064128eefc, 13b504bfb9, 6f50e695d8, from branch point 568a6acfa1). The candidate changes tests only: tests/process_macos.rs, the macOS counterpart of the Linux-only tests/process_reap.rs; a nested-job case in tests/process_windows.rs; and #[cfg(unix)] on bake-cli's print_mode test helpers. No product code changed. HEAD 519a202b13 contains the candidate. There, from a clean checkout, the Intel x86_64 macOS native preflight passed 4 gates, and its rust gate ran process_macos's 10 cases, with its 2 subprocess bodies ignored. The Linux preflight passed 33 gates under umask 022, with actionlint and runtime skipped; under umask 077 it failed scripts-unit and rust-package on the unpacked bake-rs binary's mode, which no slice touched. On the slice branch, process_macos passed in seven more Mac runs, and Linux Clippy, the Linux workspace tests, and cross-target Clippy passed. The first Mac run failed in the build on the runner's open-file limit. No Windows test ran, so the nested-job case and the README's 'a job breakaway' phrase it questions are unverified. Apple Silicon is cross-target Clippy only, and the worker's negative controls kept no logs. This record does not supersede 2026-10-14-persistent-settings-credentials, which covers settings and credential storage APIs, not process ownership. Before push the stack was rebased onto develop c5f02c476a (scope 12 web tools and hooks, scope 15 commands), which changed every hash: this record's candidate c2144d52a5 became 97d2c60707 and its base 4703b27537 became c5f02c476a, with the fixture bytes unchanged. The runs above at 519a202b13 are pre-rebase. A second run set at bfdbbcb875, the rebased stack with three integration commits on top (Windows lint fixes in the scope 12 and 15 code, D41's inconclusive loopback timeout, and Never replay classes for web_search and web_fetch), passed: the Linux preflight's 33 gates (actionlint and the TypeScript runtime skipped; 2534 Cargo tests, 6 ignored; PTY 58/58), the Intel macOS native preflight's 4 gates (2512, 6 ignored; PTY 56/56), and cross-target Clippy for Windows and Apple Silicon.

results.behavior: Every tests/process_macos.rs case passed on Intel macOS: in the native preflight's rust gate at HEAD (10 passed, 2 ignored, 14.06 s), five times in a row and once in the full crate suite at 13b504bfb9, and in the full crate suite at 6f50e695d8, each 10 passed and 2 ignored in 13.53 to 13.56 s. The file is byte-identical at HEAD, the candidate, and both slice commits. macOS has no child subreaper, so each command starts the test binary's own holder_case in the background. The holder moves itself to a process group of its own (setpgid(0, 0)) and starts sleep 1000 as its child back in the command's group. A killed member therefore stays a zombie in the group, listed by proc_listpids(PROC_PGRP_ONLY), until the test releases the holder. The holder then sends it SIGUSR1, reaps it, and reports how it ended. The leader's state is read with waitid(WEXITED | WNOHANG | WNOWAIT), without reaping it. The cases run one at a time under a SERIAL lock, and a 300 s watchdog ends an unreleased member. an_aborted_exec_waits_for_its_process_group_without_a_limit: an aborted call does not return for 6.5 s while its killed member is a zombie in the group. a_timed_out_exec_waits_for_its_process_group: the same for a timeout. a_dropped_call_is_settled_by_its_own_owner_only: a dropped call's tree is settled under its own WorkGate. shutdown_waits_for_a_cancelled_bash_call_group: AgentSession shutdown waits for a cancelled bash call's group. a_normal_exit_leaves_its_background_running_and_never_signals_it: a normal exit's member later ends by SIGUSR1, not by any owner signal. an_armed_tree_keeps_its_leader_unreaped: a tree that may still be signalled keeps its leader unreaped. an_escaped_descendant_is_neither_killed_nor_awaited: a setsid descendant is neither killed nor awaited. a_lost_leader_identity_suppresses_every_signal: a leader reaped by the test suppresses every signal. a_closing_owner_refuses_the_call: a closed owner refuses the call. a_failed_spawn_leaves_nothing_to_settle: a failed spawn leaves nothing to settle. holder_case and lost_identity_case are #[ignore] subprocess bodies that the cases start; they do not run on their own. After the run at 6f50e695d8, a ps check printed 'no strays': no holder_case, lost_identity_case, or sleep 1000 process was left on the Mac. The slice-branch Mac runs tested commits whose trees differ from the candidate's: the base 4703b27537 has 9 commits after the branch point 568a6acfa1.

results.behavior: The Windows process owner's cases in tests/process_windows.rs: powershell_paths_are_quoted, a_normal_exit_leaves_its_background_running, an_abort_ends_and_awaits_the_whole_job, the_owners_death_before_detach_ends_the_tree, and the candidate's an_abort_ends_a_nested_job_and_nothing_breaks_away. helper_case and nested_case are #[ignore] subprocess bodies. The file is #![cfg(windows)], so both HEAD rust gates ran its binary with 0 tests. In the new case, PowerShell starts nested_case inside the call's kill-on-close job. The helper asks for a child with CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB and expects it to be refused. It then creates a job that allows breakaway, assigns itself to it, and starts one child there and one with CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB. After the abort, the test requires the call to return aborted and killed with both nested children already exited. The expectations come from Microsoft's Nested Jobs and Process Creation Flags pages. The expected ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5) is the worker's prediction: the page names no error code. The file compiles and lints for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (cross-target Clippy at HEAD and at the slice head). The candidate adds Win32_System_JobObjects to the windows-sys Windows dev-dependency.

missingEvidence.what: Whether 'a job breakaway' belongs in the bake-process description
missingEvidence.reason: rust/README.md line 160, the bake-process row, lists 'a job breakaway' among the ways a descendant leaves the owned tree. The crate docs in rust/crates/bake-process/src/lib.rs line 54 say the same. But windows_job.rs set_kill_on_close sets only JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, documented as 'the only limit set on it'. Per Microsoft's Process Creation Flags page, a breakaway then needs JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK, which this job never sets, so a breakaway from it should be refused. The phrase may be wrong. Confirming that needs a Windows run of an_abort_ends_a_nested_job_and_nothing_breaks_away, which has not happened, so the text is unchanged.

missingEvidence.what: Windows runtime evidence for the process owner
missingEvidence.reason: No Windows host was available, so no case in tests/process_windows.rs has run: not the three earlier cases, not the path-quoting test, and not the new nested-job case. If the owner's ledger does not count nested jobs' processes, the new case would fail with 'the call returned while a nested job's process ran'. Windows confinement stays refused by default and unqualified.
The macOS evidence is from one Intel x86_64 Mac (XNU 12377, macOS 26.7.1). aarch64-apple-darwin is cross-target Clippy only.

missingEvidence.what: A macOS counterpart of process_reap.rs's pid-1 case
missingEvidence.reason: as_pid_1_the_owner_reaps_the_groups_orphans runs on Linux only. macOS has no PID namespace, so no macOS case covers the owner reaping a group's orphaned zombies as pid 1.

missingEvidence.what: Other ways a macOS process leaves the tree
missingEvidence.reason: The escape case covers setsid only. A launchd job, launchctl submit, or a process another service starts is untested and, like setsid, outside the owner by design.

missingEvidence.what: A killed macOS member whose parent is inside the group
missingEvidence.reason: The cases observe a member whose parent, the holder, is outside the group. A killed member whose parent is inside the group is reaped by launchd right after the kill, so its wait cannot be observed. The worker report says it runs the same owner path.
Both Linux preflights skipped actionlint (1.7.12 or later not on PATH) and runtime (no runtime source changed).
